newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks deflate to close just down.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks deflate to close just down.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2414 +9 US 30yr cl 6.41 -0.03
*Stocks end just off, profit takers ensure flat finish to day despite early record high. Volume 442.11 million shares, value A$819.62 million, 1117 stocks traded, 332 steady, 415 up, 370 down.
Australian shares deflated in the afternoon to close just lower on Thursday as profit-takers pricked a record-breaking bubble formed in the morning session.

Inspired by Wall Street's seemingly charmed run of ever-higher finishes, enthusiastic buyers ensured the key indicator hurdled the 2,400 point barrier early. It peaked at 2,406.2 at about 10.15 a.m. (2345 GMT) before the temptation to cash in on the rapid gains of the last week proved too great.
By 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 0.2 points lower at 2,392.5, barely changed from Wednesday's close.
December share price index futures were nine points higher at 2,414, a 21.5 point premium to the index.
Traders said the slicing of early gains had failed to shock, given the run-up in the last week.
"There were no surprises here this afternoon," said a Sydney broker, noting that of the sectors making the early running, only the banks had managed to secure meaningful gains by day's end.
"The banks were the only sector standing at the end. National Australia Bank was the performer there after its profit figures."
National Australia Bank reported a 6.8 percent higher full year net profit of A$2.1 billion. Traders liked what they saw and pushed its shares to a record high of A$14.22.

The upbeat tone on bank profits saw ANZ Bank shares again break into record territory, reaching a high of A$7.84. On Wednesday, ANZ Bank reported its own 6.7 percent higher full year net profit of A$1.12 billion.
Westpac Banking Corp also gained ground on the day, closing one percent higher at A$7.33.
CRA was the standout among resources, ending higher after a day of choppy, yo-yo like trade.
Major miner MIM also attracted plenty of attention, topping turnover with 23.99 million shares traded.
Brokers said institutional investor demand for the stock had been fuelled by a recent U.S. roadshow.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 11 to 10, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trading was quite active as traders covered positions early while options trade was at moderate levels.
Total options traded 42,852 (56,211)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 10,494 (8,173)

In other local markets, Australian bonds spent another session rotating in a narrow range, taking a back-seat to the gyrations in both the local dollar and equities market. By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.12 percent.
The Australian dollar stormed to six-year highs as a horde of offshore and options buyers swept aside chart barriers.

Months of range trading were eclipsed in a single day of spectacular action as a break of key resistance galvanised funds and investment banks from all quarters, triggering panic stoploss buying from options dealers. By 5.15 pm (0615 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.8080/85,up sharply on Wednesday's level.
